threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and initial task ownership for the playbook project.

messages.text: Hi team, kicking off the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout. We have 30 days to design and pilot a standardised playbook that aligns sales and contact centre processes. The goal is to improve customer experience and increase conversion rates. We need to confirm scope, define success metrics, and lock in task ownership for T1 through T4. Let's start by reviewing A4 (Pilot KPIs and Performance Tracking Sheet) and agreeing on what success looks like for the pilot phase.

Thanks for the clear kickoff. I've reviewed the project scope and I think we should focus on three core KPIs for the pilot: conversion rate improvement, average handling time consistency, and first-contact resolution rate. These align with what we track in our existing CRM and will show whether the playbook actually drives business impact. I can own T2 (qualification checklist) and T4 (email and chat templates). What timeline are we looking at for drafts?

Good thinking on the KPIs. I'd add one more: quality score based on the monitoring checklist we'll define later. That gives us a balanced view of speed, accuracy, and compliance. For timelines, I'm thinking T1 (journey mapping) and T3 (call scripts) need to be drafted by end of week, so we have time for review and refinement. T2 and T4 can follow by mid-next week. Does that work for you?

I can take T1 and T3. I'll start mapping the current journeys for inbound and outbound interactions. For T3, I'll pull the top 5 contact reasons from our volume data and draft scripts. I'll need to validate the journeys with someone from sales though—should I loop in 29962 or 379361 for that?

I can help validate the journeys. Let's sync early next week once you have a draft. For the scripts, I'd suggest we also think about how they connect to the qualification checklist—there's a handoff point there that needs to be smooth.

Exactly. That's why T2 and T3 need to be reviewed together. 29962, once you draft the qualification checklist, 269042 can align it with the scripts. Let me also confirm: are we all comfortable with the four KPIs (conversion rate, handling time, first-contact resolution, quality score) as our success criteria for D1?

I think those KPIs make sense. One question though—how are we defining 'quality score'? Is that based on the monitoring checklist, or something else? I want to make sure we're measuring the right things.

Good question. Quality score will be based on the monitoring checklist we'll define in TH3. For now, let's assume it covers compliance, script adherence, and customer satisfaction indicators. We'll refine that once we have the checklist drafted. Does that work?
I'm still a bit unclear on how the qualification checklist connects to the email templates. Can we clarify that in the next sync? I want to make sure I'm not duplicating effort when I work on T4.

The qualification checklist is for the initial discovery call or email. The email templates in T4 are for follow-up, closing, and escalation stages. So they're sequential, not overlapping. I'll make sure the checklist references the email templates so it's clear. Does that help?
Yes, that helps. Thanks for clarifying.

Alright, let me summarise for D1 and D2. D1: We agree on four KPIs—conversion rate, handling time consistency, first-contact resolution, and quality score. D2: Task ownership is as follows: 269042 owns T1 and T3 (due end of week), 29962 owns T2 and T4 (due mid-next week). 356759, are you comfortable supporting T4 if needed? And does everyone agree with these assignments?
I'm good with this. I'll have the checklist and templates drafted by mid-next week. 356759, I'll loop you in early so you can review and add any sales-specific language.
Confirmed. I'll start the journey mapping today and have a draft by Thursday. I'll also pull the top 5 contact reasons and start on the scripts.
Yes, I can support. I'll review the templates and make sure they fit with how we handle follow-ups on the sales side.

Perfect. So D1 and D2 are locked in. Next steps: 269042 drafts T1 and T3 by end of week, 29962 drafts T2 and T4 by mid-next week. We'll review those in TH2. Let's also schedule a quick sync for Monday to align on the journey mapping before 269042 finalises it.
Sounds good. I'll be ready to review the templates once they're drafted.
Great. TH1 is now closed. D1 and D2 confirmed. Moving forward with the drafts. See you all in TH2 for the script and checklist review.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise scripts, qualification checklist, and CRM guidelines.

messages.text: Posting the draft versions for async review. I've completed the Sales Qualification and Needs Analysis Checklist (A2) and initial email and chat templates (A5). The checklist covers key qualification questions for discovery calls and includes data points we need to capture in the CRM. The templates cover introduction, follow-up, closing, and escalation stages. Please review and flag any gaps or compliance concerns. I'll also need 269042 to validate that the checklist works with the call scripts.

Thanks for posting. I've reviewed the checklist and it aligns well with the call scripts I drafted. The qualification questions flow naturally into the script for the discovery call. One thing I noticed: the checklist asks for 'budget confirmation' but the script doesn't explicitly prompt for it. Should we add that to the script, or is it optional?

Good catch. Budget confirmation should be in the script, but it's sensitive—we don't want to ask too early. Let me revise the script to include it as a soft question in the needs analysis phase. I'll update A5 and repost by EOD.

I've reviewed both A2 and A5. The checklist is solid and the templates are clear. One compliance note: we need to ensure the scripts include the required consumer protection disclosures. I don't see those explicitly in the current version. Can you add a section at the end of each script that covers the mandatory disclosures? Also, I'll need to loop in the compliance officer for sign-off before we move to pilot.
Understood. I'll add a compliance section to each script template. What are the key disclosures we need to include? I want to make sure I get them right.

The main ones are: confirmation of consent to record (if applicable), data privacy statement, and cancellation/withdrawal rights. I'll send you a template separately. Once you integrate those, we'll be ready for compliance sign-off.

I've looked at the email templates. They're good overall, but I'm wondering if we should add a template for 'no decision yet' follow-ups. Sometimes prospects need more time, and we should have a standard way to re-engage them without being too pushy.
That's a good idea. I'll add a 'nurture' template for prospects who need more time. I'll include it in the revised A5.

I also want to flag something on the CRM guidelines (A3). The checklist references mandatory fields, but I need to make sure those fields are actually available in our current CRM setup. Should we validate this before we finalise A3?

Yes, that's critical. I'll check with the CRM admin to confirm which fields are available and which ones we might need to configure. I'll also make sure A3 aligns with what's actually in the system. Let me do that by tomorrow and report back.

Perfect. Once I get the compliance section from 8337 and the CRM field validation, I'll do a final revision of A2 and A5. I'm targeting EOD tomorrow for the updated versions. Then we can move to sign-off for D3 and D4.

Sounds good. Once I validate the CRM fields and you integrate the compliance language, I'll review and sign off on D3 (qualification checklist) and D4 (scripts and templates). We should be ready by end of day tomorrow. 269042, can you also do a final review of the scripts against the journeys you mapped?
Yes, I'll do that. I'll make sure the scripts match the journey steps and that the handoff points are clear.

Great. So the plan is: 29962 revises A2 and A5 by EOD tomorrow with compliance language and nurture template. I validate CRM fields and send compliance template by EOD tomorrow. 269042 reviews scripts against journeys by EOD tomorrow. Then I do final sign-off on D3 and D4. Everyone good?
Confirmed. I'll have the revisions ready.
Confirmed. I'll review and flag any gaps.
Perfect. TH2 is on track. Once we have the final versions and sign-offs, we'll move to TH3 to lock in the training plan and quality monitoring process.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in training approach, schedule, and quality monitoring process.

messages.text: Sharing the draft training plan (A7) and quality monitoring checklist (A6) for feedback. The training plan outlines objectives, content, and a schedule that fits within current shift patterns. We're proposing two waves: one for the pilot group (week 2) and one for the broader rollout (week 4). The quality checklist maps to the key behaviours in the scripts and includes compliance checkpoints. Please review for feasibility and let me know if the schedule works with your teams.

I've reviewed A7. The schedule looks workable, but I have a concern: the training sessions are scheduled for 2 hours each, and I'm not sure we can pull people off the phones for that long without impacting service levels. Can we break it into shorter sessions, maybe 45 minutes each, spread over a few days?

That's a fair point. Let me revise A7 to break the training into 45-minute modules. We can do the core content in one session and then follow up with scenario-based practice in a second session. That way, people get the key concepts without being away from their desks for too long.
I've also reviewed A6. The quality checklist is comprehensive, but I'm wondering about the review cadence. How often are we planning to review calls? Weekly? And who's responsible for the reviews?

Good question. For the pilot phase, I'm proposing weekly reviews of a sample of calls (maybe 5-10 per team). The contact centre supervisor and I will do the reviews together, and we'll provide coaching feedback to the agents. Once we move to full rollout, we can adjust the cadence based on what we learn. Does that work?

I'm looking at A7 and I'm a bit concerned about the content. It seems focused on contact centre processes, but we also need to train the sales team on how to use the qualification checklist and the new email templates. Should we have a separate training track for sales account managers?

You're right. I should have been clearer. A7 includes two tracks: one for contact centre agents and one for sales account managers. The sales track covers the qualification checklist, email templates, and escalation paths. Let me make sure that's explicit in the revised version.
That makes sense. One more thing: should we include a session on how to handle objections or difficult calls? I think that would be useful for both teams.
Good idea. I'll add a module on handling objections and difficult scenarios. That can be part of the scenario-based practice session. Let me revise A7 to include that.

On A6, I think the checklist is solid, but I want to make sure we're not being too rigid. The scripts are guidelines, not scripts to be read word-for-word, right? So the quality checklist should focus on the key behaviours and outcomes, not exact wording.

Exactly. The scripts are templates, not rigid scripts. The quality checklist should focus on whether the agent covered the key points, asked the right questions, and handled the interaction professionally. I'll make sure A6 reflects that distinction.
That's important. We don't want agents to feel like they're robots reading from a script. They need flexibility to adapt to the customer's needs while still following the key steps.

Agreed. So here's the plan: I'll revise A7 to include shorter training modules (45 minutes each), separate tracks for contact centre and sales, and a module on handling objections. I'll also revise A6 to focus on key behaviours and outcomes rather than exact wording. I'll have the updated versions by EOD tomorrow. Then I need sign-off from the customer service manager on A6 before we can move forward. Can someone loop them in?
I'll loop in the customer service manager. They'll want to review A6 to make sure it aligns with our quality standards.
Thanks. Once I have the revised versions ready and the customer service manager signs off on A6, we can lock in D5 and D6. That should be by end of day tomorrow. Everyone good with that timeline?
Good with me. I'll be ready to start training prep once A7 is finalised.
Confirmed. I'll get the customer service manager's feedback and report back.
Perfect. TH3 is on track. Once D5 and D6 are locked in, we'll move to TH4 to plan the pilot rollout and define escalation paths.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot rollout, including escalation paths and dashboards.

messages.text: Pilot teams have been selected and we need to lock in the scope, duration, and reporting approach. We're proposing a 2-week pilot with one contact centre team (10 agents) and one sales pod (5 account managers). The pilot will run in parallel with business as usual, so we can compare KPIs before and after. We also need to define escalation criteria for high-value leads and confirm the dashboard metrics (A4). Let's align on D7 and D8 today.

I'm good with the pilot scope and duration. Two weeks gives us enough time to see patterns without running too long. For the escalation criteria, I'm thinking we should escalate leads that meet these criteria: deal value over a certain threshold (let's say 50k), strategic accounts, or complex requirements. What do you think?

That makes sense. Let's also add 'customer has escalated a complaint' as a criterion. And we need to define the SLA for escalation—how quickly should the sales team respond to an escalated lead from the contact centre?
Good point. I'd suggest 4 hours for high-value leads and 24 hours for standard escalations. That gives us time to respond without losing momentum.

I'm also good with the pilot scope. On the dashboard metrics, I want to make sure we're tracking the right things. Are we capturing conversion rate, handling time, first-contact resolution, and quality score? And are those metrics available in the current CRM?

Yes, those are the four KPIs we agreed on in TH1. I've validated with the CRM admin that all four metrics can be pulled from existing fields. Conversion rate and first-contact resolution are already tracked. Handling time is available from call logs. Quality score will be calculated from the monitoring checklist. So we're good on data availability.

I have a question about the pilot scope. Are we including all types of interactions (inbound, outbound, follow-up) or just a subset? I want to make sure we're testing the full playbook, not just one part of it.

Good question. We're including all types of interactions in the pilot. The contact centre team will use the new scripts for inbound calls, and the sales pod will use the new qualification checklist and email templates for outbound and follow-up. That way, we're testing the full end-to-end playbook.
That makes sense. One thing I'm wondering: how are we handling the transition from contact centre to sales? Is there a handoff process we need to test?

Yes, that's part of T10. We're defining the escalation paths and handoff process. The contact centre will use the qualification checklist to determine if a lead should be escalated to sales. If it meets the criteria, they'll send it to the sales pod with all the relevant information. The sales team will then follow up within the agreed SLA.
Exactly. So the handoff is part of the playbook. During the pilot, we'll monitor how smoothly the handoffs happen and whether the SLAs are being met. That will be one of our key metrics for success.
I want to flag something on the reporting. We're planning to track KPIs weekly, right? Who's responsible for pulling the data and creating the reports?

Good point. I'll own the weekly KPI reporting during the pilot. I'll pull the data from the CRM and create a summary report that we'll review in our weekly check-in. That way, we can spot any issues early and adjust if needed.

Good. So to summarise for D7 and D8: D7 is the pilot scope (2 weeks, one contact centre team, one sales pod, all interaction types). D8 is the escalation criteria (deal value >50k, strategic accounts, complex requirements, escalated complaints) with SLAs (4 hours for high-value, 24 hours for standard). Does everyone agree?
Confirmed. D7 and D8 are locked in. I'll document the escalation criteria and SLAs in the playbook (A1) and share with the pilot teams. We'll kick off the pilot next Monday. Everyone ready?
Ready. I'll make sure the contact centre team is prepped and knows what to expect.
Ready on the sales side. I'll brief the pod on the new qualification checklist and escalation process.
Great. TH4 is closed. D7 and D8 confirmed. Pilot kicks off Monday. We'll do weekly KPI check-ins to monitor progress. Next thread (TH5) will be for pilot results and go-live planning.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate learnings from pilot and confirm go-live plan for full rollout.

messages.text: Pilot is complete. Preliminary KPI results are in A4. Overall, the playbook is working well. Conversion rate improved by 8%, handling time decreased by 12%, first-contact resolution improved by 6%, and quality score averaged 87%. These results meet our success criteria. Now we need to confirm that we're ready for full rollout and finalise the communication plan (A8) and consolidated playbook (A1). Let's review the results and lock in D1 (reconfirm success criteria met).

Excellent results. The 8% conversion improvement is significant, and the handling time reduction shows the playbook is efficient. I'm confident these results support moving to full rollout. I've also started working on the communication plan (A8) to brief all teams on the rollout timeline and expectations.

The results look solid. One thing I want to highlight: the quality score of 87% is good, but we had a few calls where agents didn't follow the escalation criteria correctly. I've documented those in the pilot report. We should include a refresher on escalation in the full rollout training.

Good catch. I'll make sure the escalation process is emphasised in the full rollout training. That's a critical handoff point, so we need to get it right. Let me also consolidate the pilot learnings into the final playbook (A1).
The results are impressive. I'm ready to support the full rollout. One question: are we rolling out to all teams at once, or are we staggering it by team?

Good question. I'm proposing a staggered rollout by team over 2 weeks. That way, we can monitor KPIs and provide targeted coaching where needed. We'll start with the teams that are most ready and move to others as they complete training. Does that work?
Staggered rollout makes sense. It reduces the risk of a big drop in KPIs if something goes wrong. I'll work with 8337 to schedule the training waves and make sure we have coaching support in place.
I agree with the staggered approach. It also gives us time to gather feedback from each wave and adjust if needed before moving to the next team.

The pilot results are great. I'm wondering about the communication plan (A8). What's the key message we want to send to the teams? I want to make sure we're framing this as a positive change, not just a new process to follow.

That's a good point. The key message should be that the playbook is designed to make their jobs easier and help them serve customers better. The pilot results show that it works—faster handling, better outcomes, and clearer processes. I'll make sure A8 emphasises those benefits.

Exactly. The communication plan should highlight the pilot results and explain how the playbook benefits both the teams and the customers. I'll review A8 once 29962 has it drafted and make sure the messaging is consistent.

So here's the plan for full rollout: We confirm D1 (pilot KPIs meet success criteria). I consolidate the final playbook (A1) with pilot learnings. 29962 finalises the communication plan (A8). We schedule training waves over 2 weeks with staggered rollout. I'll also prepare a post-rollout monitoring plan to track KPIs and provide coaching. Can everyone confirm they're ready to move forward?
Confirmed. I'll have A8 ready by EOD tomorrow. I'm also ready to support the training waves and monitor KPIs during rollout.
Confirmed. I'll support the training and coaching during rollout. I'll also monitor the escalation process closely to make sure teams are following the criteria correctly.
Ready to go. I'll help with the training and support the sales teams during the rollout.
Confirmed. I'm ready to support the rollout and help with any questions from the teams.

Perfect. D1 is confirmed—pilot KPIs meet our success criteria and we're moving to full rollout. I'll have the final playbook (A1) ready by EOD tomorrow. Training waves start next week. Let's do a final check-in before we kick off to make sure everyone is aligned. Great work, team. The pilot results show that this playbook is going to make a real difference.
